Samples of harbor seal, elephant seal, and California sea lion vibrissae were collected and analyzed using CT scanning, microscopy, and 3D scanning techniques.
The seal blade designs incorporated undulations on the suction side to match the parameters of the seal vibrissae, while keeping the pressure side largely unaffected.
Computational fluid dynamics simulations were conducted using the NASA Glenn-HT code with the SST-transition enabled two-equation model.
The baseline untreated turbine blade showed separation at negative and high positive incidence angles, which the seal blade designs aimed to mitigate.
At a Reynolds number of 100,000, the seal blades showed consistent performance improvements over the baseline configuration.
The total pressure loss coefficient was reduced by up to 50% for the seal blades compared to the untreated baseline.
Hotwire surveys in the wake of the seal blades showed a reduction in turbulence intensity by up to 4.5%.
The seal blades exhibited insensitivity to incidence angle, maintaining improved performance at negative, zero, and positive incidence angles.
The wind tunnel pitot surveys on the Sin1R0P5 seal blade showed good agreement with the computational fluid dynamics results.
The hotwire surveys on the Sin1R0P5 seal blade suggested the potential for noise reduction through a reduction in broadband frequency content.
A fuel burn reduction of approximately 5% could be achieved for a fixed-wing aircraft application using the seal blade concept.
The researchers suggest that future work could explore optimizing the undulation parameters along the chord and investigating the effect on acoustics.
The flexibility of the seal whiskers was not fully captured in the current study and could be an area for further investigation.
The seal blade concept could also be beneficial for fan blades on fixed-wing aircraft or rotors and tails on rotorcraft.
The large thickness-to-chord ratio of the variable speed power turbine blade provided enough volume for potential internal flow control activities.
